title: Ambiguous S3 subresource query lets a bucket tagger replace the bucket policy
summary:
# Ambiguous S3 subresource query lets a bucket tagger replace the bucket policy

## Summary

SeaweedFS routes an S3 `PUT` containing both `policy` and `tagging` subresources to the bucket-policy handler, while its IAM action resolver authorizes the same request only as `s3:PutBucketTagging`. A low-privilege principal delegated tag management on another tenant's bucket can therefore install an arbitrary bucket policy. The reproduced policy exposed a previously private victim object to an anonymous request.

## Impact and affected scope

- **Type:** Broken access control
- **Affected component:** SigV4-authenticated SeaweedFS S3 gateway bucket subresource handling
- **Preconditions:** A valid S3 identity with `s3:PutBucketTagging` on the victim bucket but no bucket-policy permission
- **Verified revision:** `8dcdb70594ae9e9c2ac07aa6d497f38d8c580448` on 27 August 2026
- **Affected release range:** `<= 4.44`, as entered by the maintainer; patched version not yet specified

The demonstrated policy granted anonymous read, write, and delete actions to the victim bucket's objects. The report does not claim impact outside the affected bucket authorization boundary.

## Technical details

Gorilla routing selects the bucket-policy handler because the `policy` route is registered first and still matches when extra query keys are present. The independently ordered action resolver checks `tagging` first, so IAM authorizes only `s3:PutBucketTagging`. The selected policy handler then persists the supplied policy without a second policy-management check.

Relevant code:

- `weed/s3api/s3api_server.go:899` - registers the bucket subresource routes.
- `weed/s3api/s3_action_resolver.go:148,196` - resolves the ambiguous request as tag management.
- `weed/s3api/s3_iam_middleware.go:304` and `weed/s3api/auth_credentials.go:2659` - authorize the resolved action.
- `weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_policy_handlers.go:73,239` - stores and applies the policy body.

## Reproduction

Run this only on an authorized disposable host with Go 1.26 and Python 3. Build the verified revision:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs.git
cd seaweedfs
git checkout 8dcdb70594ae9e9c2ac07aa6d497f38d8c580448
go build -trimpath -o weed-poc ./weed
mkdir -p poc-data poc-tmp
```

Save this as `s3-poc.json`:

```json
{
  "identities": [
    {
      "name": "victim-admin",
      "credentials": [
        {"accessKey": "victim-admin", "secretKey": "victim-secret"}
      ],
      "actions": ["Admin"]
    },
    {
      "name": "tagger",
      "credentials": [
        {"accessKey": "tagger", "secretKey": "tagger-secret"}
      ],
      "policyNames": ["VictimTagOnly"]
    }
  ],
  "policies": [
    {
      "name": "VictimTagOnly",
      "content": "{\"Version\":\"2012-10-17\",\"Statement\":[{\"Effect\":\"Allow\",\"Action\":[\"s3:PutBucketTagging\"],\"Resource\":[\"arn:aws:s3:::victim-bucket\"]}]}"
    }
  ]
}
```

Start the real mini deployment:

```sh
TMPDIR="$PWD/poc-tmp" WEED_TELEMETRY=false ./weed-poc mini \
  -dir="$PWD/poc-data" \
  -ip=127.0.0.1 -ip.bind=127.0.0.1 \
  -master.port=19333 -volume.port=19340 -filer.port=18888 \
  -s3.port=18333 -s3.port.iceberg=0 -s3.port.lance=0 \
  -s3.config="$PWD/s3-poc.json" -metricsPort=19326 \
  -webdav=false -admin.ui=false -master.telemetry=false \
  -master.volumeSizeLimitMB=64 -volume.preStopSeconds=0 \
  >seaweedfs-poc.log 2>&1 &
```
